disclaimer: Educational guidance compiled from public hobby sources (June 2026). Prices, fees, and grading tiers change often — always confirm current numbers and check live sold comps before selling or grading.

gradeMultiples.vintage: Vintage WOTC (1999–2003): PSA 10 ≈ 5–10× raw NM (10×+ for elite chase cards); PSA 10 ≈ 5–7× a PSA 9. Gem-mint survivors are genuinely scarce, so the 10 carries the value.
gradeMultiples.modern: Modern Scarlet & Violet (2023–2025): PSA 10 ≈ 1.5–3× raw NM; PSA 10 ≈ 1.3–2.5× a PSA 9. Big PSA-10 populations mean 10s aren't scarce.
gradeMultiples.note: Universal one-grade cliff: a PSA 9 usually sells for only 30–50% of the matching PSA 10. Cards >$100 raw see roughly +120–300% at PSA 10; cards under ~$10 raw rarely gain enough to cover grading. Japanese modern cards gem ~2–3× more often than English (~15–20% vs ~8–12%), but clean English PSA 10s often command higher prices.

gradeCandidateSignals: Modern English: raw value ≳ $75–80 (or $50+ if a clean PSA 10 looks likely)
Vintage: raw value ≳ $40 with a real shot at grading 9+ — the 10 multiple does the heavy lifting
Universal floor: worth at least ~$30 raw NM before grading is mathematically sensible
Target an expected graded value ≥ ~3× your total grading cost for reliable ROI
Centering 60/40 or better front AND back (off-centering is the #1 PSA-10 killer)
No print lines, scratches, or surface scuffs; clean glossy surface
Marquee modern alt-arts / Special Illustration Rares (Charizard, Umbreon/Moonbreon, Pikachu) are the strongest modern bets
Clean vintage holos of iconic Pokémon (Base Charizard/Blastoise/Venusaur) are the highest-ROI targets overall
Japanese raw cards are better grading bets on condition odds (tighter centering, finer holo, ~2–3× higher gem rate)
doNotGrade: Anything under ~$30 raw with no realistic appreciation — fees and shipping eat the gain
Bulk modern holos / ex cards under ~$10 raw — a stack of PSA 9s on $5 cards loses money
Commons, uncommons, and non-alt-art modern rares — high population, tiny premium
Visibly flawed cards (edge wear, bends, scratches, print lines, heavy off-centering) — these grade ≤7 and often sell at or under raw
Modern cards likely to grade 9 not 10 — a modern PSA 9 is only 0.4–0.7× the 10 and frequently won't beat raw + fees

gradingTiers.tier: Regular (cheapest active PSA, Jun 2026 — Value tiers paused)

breakEven: As of June 2026, budget roughly $30–$40 all-in per card at the cheapest realistic tier (low grading fee + a share of shipping/insurance). The graded value should exceed raw by at least ~$35 just to break even, and ideally be ≥ ~3× your total cost to justify the time and risk. PSA's sub-$30 Value tiers are paused — cheapest legit routes now are CGC Bulk (~$17), Beckett Base (~$15–25), or TAG Basic ($22); PSA's floor is Regular at $79.99 (only worth it for cards expected to clear ~$240+ graded).

marketplaces.name: eBay (US)
marketplaces.bestFor: High-value cards, graded slabs, vintage holos, and Japanese cards. Largest, most liquid global audience (~58% of Pokémon volume). Best for max price, not speed. Authenticity Guarantee on singles ≥$250.

marketplaces.name: TCGplayer
marketplaces.bestFor: Raw English singles, modern/playable cards, and bulk lots. The dedicated TCG marketplace where players buy by exact set/condition. Weak for graded slabs and Japanese cards.

marketplaces.name: Mercari (US)
marketplaces.bestFor: Raw English mid-value singles and small lots, sold fast with the cheapest US fees. Casual buyer base; not ideal for premium slabs.

marketplaces.name: Whatnot
marketplaces.bestFor: Speed — moving lower/mid inventory fast via live auctions; bulk breaks. Live urgency can spike prices with a big audience.

marketplaces.name: Cardmarket (EU)
marketplaces.bestFor: The European audience and the cheapest venue for high-value cards thanks to the €100 cap. Strong for English and Japanese singles within Europe.

marketplaces.name: COMC
marketplaces.bestFor: Hands-off consignment of bulk/low-value English singles. Cheap only if you recycle credit into buying; cash-out is pricey.

rawEnglish: TCGplayer — dedicated player audience, fair pricing, best for volume
Mercari — cheapest at ~10% flat, fast for mid-value singles
Whatnot / COMC — for bulk you want gone
gradedEnglish: eBay — most liquid market for slabs, standard for max price
Whatnot — strong for mid-value slabs with live viewership
japanese: eBay — by far the largest global buyer base searching Japanese sets
Cardmarket — cheapest fees if you can serve EU buyers
Mercari Japan / Yahoo! Auctions Japan via Buyee for Japan-native demand
